newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares post fourth record close in a row.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares post fourth record close in a row.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss share indices ended at a new record high, the fourth consecutive record closing, just a shade off the 4,300 level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).

The market was somewhat nervous about the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting, so some profit taking could be seen off and on, dealers said. However, the possibility of an increase in U.S. interest rates was considered minimal.
Prospects remained favourable as buying interest was lively after several upgrades of the Swiss market by U.S. brokers, a trader noted.
* The SMI ended up 13.7 points, or 0.32 percent, to 4,296.5.
* Insurer Winterthur lost one franc to 848.
* Surveillance jumped 135 francs, or 4.29 percent, to 3,280, on buying by Geneva-based investors. One trader noted the share may have been propelled by a forthcoming study.
* Swissair suffed from a downgrade by a bank and slumped 15 francs to 1,285.
